newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia panel cuts number missing from riots.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia panel cuts number missing from riots.

text.p: Indonesia's official National Commission on Human Rights has revised down to 30 from 74 the number of people missing since the July 27 riots in the capital, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Thursday.
The daily quoted commission member Albert Hasibuan as telling reporters that 30 people were still missing after the riots in the capital, the worst in more than 20 years.
"After thoroughly cross-checking reports and information we have been receiving, we conclude that there are still 30 persons missing," he was quoted as saying.
In its preliminary report on August 31, the commission said at least five people had died, 149 were injured and 74 had been reported missing.
The commission has never released details on the missing, who are thought to include political activists and others who went underground after authorities cracked down on dissidents.
The government said only four people died in the riots, and neither the government nor the military has acknowledged any missing people.
State Secretary Murdiono called on the commission to prove its findings with acceptable evidence.
Hasibuan was quoted as saying the number of casualties from the riots, which started after police raided the headquarters of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), remained the same.
Supporters of ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri had been occupying the building since she was removed from office by party rivals at a government-backed congress in June.
Hasibuan said the new figure for missing people was still provisional and could drop further.
Sources close to the commission have said they expect it could drop to around 10 by the time the rights body releases its final report later this month.
It is expected to find that many of these were wrongly listed as missing or have subsequently come out of hiding.
